title: EKG electrode placement: chest leads V1 to V6 (anterior)
attribution: 3D anatomy from Z-Anatomy, built on BodyParts3D (CC BY-SA). Rendered in Blender, with surface detail added by an image model.

rows: Placement
Fourth intercostal space at the right border of the sternum.
Used for
Chest lead V1. With V2 it looks at the interventricular septum from the front.
hy: To find the fourth space, feel for the sternal angle. The second rib joins the sternum there, so the space just below it is the second. Count down two more.

rows: Placement
Fourth intercostal space at the left border of the sternum, level with V1.
Used for
Chest lead V2. With V1 it looks at the interventricular septum from the front.
Placement
Midway between V2 and V4, so V4 is placed first.
Used for
Chest lead V3. With V4 it looks at the anterior wall of the left ventricle.
Placement
Fifth intercostal space on the left midclavicular line.
Used for
Chest lead V4. With V3 it looks at the anterior wall of the left ventricle, near the apex.
Placement
Left anterior axillary line, at the same horizontal level as V4. It does not follow the fifth intercostal space, which climbs toward the back.
Used for
Chest lead V5. With V6 it looks at the lateral wall of the left ventricle.
Placement
Left midaxillary line, at the same horizontal level as V4 and V5.
Used for
Chest lead V6. With V5 it looks at the lateral wall of the left ventricle.

structures.name: RA (right arm)
objects: EKG electrode RA on the torso (built)

rows: Placement

Right wrist, or anywhere on the right arm. For monitoring and exercise testing it may be moved to the trunk, just below the outer part of the right clavicle. A tracing made that way is marked, because it differs slightly from a standard one.
Used for

The negative pole of leads I and II and the positive pole of aVR. Together with the left arm and left leg electrodes it also forms the central terminal, the reference point against which the six chest leads are measured.
hy: Swapping the right arm and left arm electrodes turns lead I upside down, exchanges leads II and III, and exchanges aVR and aVL. The chest leads stay normal, which tells this mistake from dextrocardia.

structures.name: LA (left arm)
objects: EKG electrode LA on the torso (built)

rows: Placement
Left wrist, or anywhere on the left arm. For monitoring and exercise testing it may be moved to the trunk, just below the outer part of the left clavicle.
Used for
The positive pole of lead I and of aVL, and the negative pole of lead III.

structures.name: RL (right leg)
objects: EKG electrode RL on the torso (built)

rows: Placement
Right ankle, or anywhere on the right leg. On the trunk it may sit on the lower part of the abdomen.
Used for
The ground electrode. It is part of no lead. The machine uses it to reduce electrical noise.

structures.name: LL (left leg)
objects: EKG electrode LL on the torso (built)

rows: Placement
Left ankle, or anywhere on the left leg. On the trunk it sits on the left side below the ribs, on the anterior axillary line midway between the costal margin and the iliac crest.
Used for
The positive pole of leads II and III and of aVF.
